about: A one-time limited toro from Jeremy McDonald's Wildfire Cigar Co., named after a fly fishing term. It was the first of the company's monthly made-to-order releases and shipped in March 2026.
notes: The factory is undisclosed; Wildfire says only that it is made in the Dominican Republic. Production numbers were not announced. The maker says it starts medium and finishes full, while halfwheel's reviewer found the strength below medium.

about: A limited robusto extra from Wildfire Cigar Co. with a San Andrés wrapper and an unusual Sumatra-seed binder grown in India. It was the second of the company's monthly made-to-order releases, shipping in April 2026.
notes: The maker lists the filler as Criollo 98, Ecuadorian and Corojo; halfwheel lists Ecuadorian habano and Nicaraguan Criollo 98. Halfwheel says the Sumatra-seed binder was grown in India, while one retailer lists it as Indonesian. Production numbers were not announced.
verifyNotes: All fields confirmed against the maker page and halfwheel. Added a note that Luxury Cigar Club lists the binder as Indonesian where halfwheel says India, and added that page as a source.

about: A limited corona gorda from Wildfire Cigar Co. built around a five-year-old Ecuadorian corojo wrapper and meant to show the lighter side of the company's blending. It shipped in July 2026 as part of the monthly made-to-order series.
notes: The maker writes the name with a hyphen; halfwheel and Cigar Dojo write Radio Octave. A one-and-done run made to the number of retailer orders, with the total not disclosed.

about: The October 2026 release in Wildfire Cigar Co.'s monthly made-to-order limited series, a single robusto extra themed around unplugging from phones and screens. Its band shows a towable camper like the one in the company's trade show booths.
notes: Fifth release in the series Wildfire informally calls the Camp Counselor Enrollment Program. The maker has not published a strength rating. One retailer calls it medium-bodied and lists it as 5 1/2 x 54, while halfwheel and Cigar Dojo give 5 1/4 x 54.
verifyNotes: Blend, factory and size confirmed on halfwheel and Cigar Dojo. Strength left null: the maker's site does not list this cigar and no source rates strength. Added a note on the retailer's differing size and added that page as a source.

about: Wildfire Cigar Co.'s first regular production line from 2021, since discontinued and brought back in August 2026 as a reworked limited edition. The new version is a box-pressed toro made in the Dominican Republic with a different filler blend.
notes: Details shown are the 2026 limited version. The original 2021 line was made at Joya de Nicaragua in Corona Gorda (5 5/8 x 46), Robusto (5 1/4 x 50) and Toro (6 1/4 x 52), also with a Mexican claro wrapper, and is discontinued. Wildfire calls the new one medium-bodied.
verifyNotes: No changes. Strength is null because the maker's site does not list this cigar and sources give body only. Halfwheel's 2021 and 2026 articles disagree on the original line's binder and filler; the record describes the 2026 version.

factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
about: The debut limited edition from Jeremy McDonald's Wildfire Cigar Co., a single Churchill made at Joya de Nicaragua. It shipped in September 2021 and was limited to 750 boxes of 10.
notes: Limited to 7,500 cigars. Strength, body and flavors come from halfwheel's review, which found it below medium strength until the final third. It scored 89 there.

factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
